content.text:
The Takeout import finished successfully, but it does not connect your API account. The archive gave you only a few days of data.

**Import status:** Succeeded. 9 files were processed and 11 records were inserted. Nothing was updated or skipped.

**What you have locally (coverage):**
- **Fitbit Takeout**
  - Steps: 2 records on 2026-10-01
  - Heart rate: 1 sample on 2026-10-01
  - Resting heart rate: 1 day, 2026-10-01
  - Weight: 1 record on 2026-10-01, but the unit is unknown, so it's excluded from unit-converted summaries
  - BMI: 1 record on 2026-10-01
  - Sleep: 1 session on 2026-10-02 (minutes asleep, minutes awake, time in bed, efficiency)
- **Google Takeout**
  - Steps: 1 record on 2026-10-03

Every other category (exercise, cardio fitness, SpO2, nutrition, and so on) has no local records. Days without data are missing, not zero.

**Warnings and unparsed files:**
- The archive contained a symbolic link, which was not extracted.
- One day of resting heart rate (2026-10-01) had no estimate and was treated as missing.
- Four files were not parsed: a sleep-log CSV, an HTML file, and a JSON file with an unrecognized structure. Three of these are counted as unsupported; the symbolic link is the fourth item. The raw files are kept on disk.

**Does this connect your API account?** No. The import only reads the archive. Your API connections are both still unconnected:
- **Google:** not connected. Google is not onboarding new projects, so the connection depends on your existing ghealth CLI setup.
- **Fitbit:** not connected. The tool reports that the legacy Fitbit Web API is scheduled to be turned off on 2026-10-30, so that route may no longer work.

If you want live data beyond this archive, you would need to connect an account separately. I can start that when you tell me which provider to use.
